story.title: Increase daily payment limits for premium customers
story.description: Increase daily payment limits for premium customers from AED 25,000 to AED 50,000 for domestic transfers. The payment-service must obtain premium eligibility and the effective account limit from account-service before accepting each payment. Keep fraud screening active through fraud-engine and use the transaction ledger in transaction-db to calculate the remaining daily allowance, including concurrent requests. Roll out the business rule behind an approved feature flag during the payments release window. Operations must confirm threshold monitoring and rollback readiness before enabling the higher limit; standard customer limits remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A premium account can submit domestic payments totaling AED 50,000 per bank-local calendar day; the next payment is declined.
A standard account retains its AED 25,000 daily limit and existing per-payment checks.
Concurrent payment submissions cannot exceed the account daily limit, and retries create one transaction ledger posting.
Every accepted payment passes fraud screening; operations approves monitoring and can restore the previous limit with the feature flag.

requirement.business_summary: Increase daily payment limit for premium customers from AED 25,000 to AED 50,000 for domestic transfers while keeping standard customer limits unchanged.
requirement.technical_summary: Payment-service will obtain premium eligibility and effective daily limit from account-service before accepting each payment, apply fraud screening via fraud-engine, and compute remaining daily allowance using transaction ledger in transaction-db (including concurrent requests). The change is gated by a feature flag; operations will monitor and can rollback via the flag.
requirement.engineering_scope: Update payment-service to query account-service for premium eligibility and dynamic daily limit, integrate with fraud-engine, use transaction-db for daily allowance calculation with concurrency handling, introduce feature flag for rollout, and adjust monitoring/rollback procedures.

tests.title: Compliance: Premium limit increase audit events capture effective limit and premium eligibility

tests.title: Operational: Feature flag rollback reverts premium limit to 25,000 AED within one minute
steps: Ensure feature flag for premium limit increase is enabled.

tests.expected: After disabling the flag, the payment is declined with a daily limit exceeded error, and the rollback is logged without service restart.

tests.summary: Selected 15 catalog tests and 8 new tests, covering 15 of 17 impacted nodes (88%); estimated effort is 13.2 hours.

frameworks.reason: PII-bearing components are impacted; the change touches customer data.

findings.text: The change makes payment-service request premium status and an effective daily limit from account-service before accepting a payment, so customer attributes are newly used inside the payment authorization decision. The purpose limitation, minimization and retention basis for that eligibility lookup, and for the profile attributes read from customer-db, should be confirmed before rollout.

Personal data traverses api-gateway and authentication-service on the same path as the new limit check, including token scope and session context. Exposure of eligibility or limit attributes in gateway logs, traces and error responses, and the scope checks enforced at authentication-service, should be reviewed.

Limit-change communications routed through notification-service rely on consent-aware delivery to verified destinations. The content of those messages, the preference lookup against customer-db, and any change in notification volume triggered by the new limit should be checked for data minimization and consent coverage.

recommendations: Confirm lawful basis, purpose limitation, minimization and retention for the premium-eligibility and effective-limit data exchanged between payment-service and account-service, including attributes sourced from customer-db.
Verify that access controls, token scopes and logging on api-gateway and authentication-service cover the new limit-check path and do not surface personal data in logs or error payloads.
Review consent and channel preferences in notification-service before any limit-change messaging, and confirm privacy regression tests exist for the affected flow.

findings.text: The change does not introduce card data into the payment limit flow, but fraud-engine is a shared screening component also used for card-not-present velocity checks. Any rule, configuration or data-flow change on that component should be assessed for its effect on the cardholder data environment, segmentation and logging.

card-service and api-gateway handle card lifecycle and card status routing adjacent to the modified payment path. Payloads, routing rules and step-up calls should be checked to confirm no cardholder data is added to the new limit-enforcement request or response chain, including calls through authentication-service.

recommendations: Confirm that no cardholder data elements are introduced into the new premium-eligibility or daily-limit payloads exchanged between payment-service, account-service and transaction-db.
Review fraud-engine rule and configuration changes for impact on card-not-present velocity screening and confirm card-data security tests still exercise the affected screening path.
Re-verify masking, encryption and access restrictions on card-service and its routing through api-gateway and authentication-service after the limit change is deployed.

frameworks.reason: financial-data components are impacted; audit-data components are impacted; the change touches financial data.

findings.text: The change alters payment authorization logic in payment-service using a premium eligibility result from account-service, which affects how financial transactions are accepted and against what limit. This is a business-rule change on a financially significant path and requires change-management evidence, control-owner approval and testing before release.

Daily allowance is computed from transaction-db with concurrency handling, so posting accuracy, idempotency and daily-total consistency are exposed. Reconciliation of ledger entries and daily totals should be performed to confirm the new calculation does not create duplicate, missing or misstated postings.

Limit decisions and eligibility outcomes should remain traceable through audit-db, with downstream effect on reporting-db projections and risk-engine and fraud-engine signals. Completeness, immutability and retention of the audit records supporting the changed rule should be verified.

recommendations: Reconcile transaction-db ledger entries and daily totals after the change, and verify idempotent posting behaviour under concurrent payment requests.
Document control-owner approval, test evidence and rollback criteria for the payment limit business-rule change in payment-service and account-service.
Verify that audit-db events for limit and eligibility decisions are complete and append-only, and confirm reporting-db projections reflect the revised limit behaviour.

findings.text: Directly changed components include payment-service, account-service, fraud-engine and transaction-db, which are high-criticality services on tier1 paths with wide downstream dependency. Service-owner approval, documented rollback criteria and release evidence should be in place before the change is promoted.

The rollout depends on a feature flag as the primary control gate. Flag ownership, default state, evaluation scope and a defined sunset should be recorded so the flag cannot be used to bypass limit enforcement or persist untracked after rollout.

Concurrency handling for daily allowance and monitoring/rollback procedures are part of the engineering scope, but observability coverage across the affected services and their downstream ledger writes should be checked. Authorization tests and operational monitoring evidence will be needed to demonstrate the change behaves as intended.

recommendations: Obtain service-owner approval and record the rollback plan for payment-service, account-service, fraud-engine and transaction-db before promotion.
Define feature-flag ownership, safe default, evaluation scope and sunset date, and confirm the flag cannot bypass limit enforcement once disabled.
Verify authorization tests, concurrency handling and operational monitoring for the affected path, and retain release evidence covering api-gateway and authentication-service interactions.
